name: Answer-Set Consistency QA Benchmark Collection (English)
description: English benchmark collection used in the Answer-Set Consistency of LLMs for Question Answering study. The collection contains four TSV files with tuples of semantically related questions (Q1-Q4) designed to test set-equivalence, containment, and partition-style consistency in question answering. The English release under data/Dataset/en contains 596 benchmark items in total, with 150 data rows in each source file. For NeurIPS 2026 ED submission, this file is a collection-level reference only; individual datasets should be submitted with the per-dataset Croissant files.

distribution.name: LC-QuAD English benchmark TSV
distribution.description: 150 benchmark items adapted from LC-QuAD-style question pairs and decompositions.

distribution.name: QAWiki English benchmark TSV
distribution.description: 150 benchmark items constructed from QAWiki-style entities and relation-preserving question rewrites.

distribution.name: SPINACH English benchmark TSV
distribution.description: 150 benchmark items derived from SPINACH-style SPARQL question seeds and rewritten into four related queries.

distribution.name: Synthetic English benchmark TSV
distribution.description: 150 synthetic benchmark items created to exercise controlled set-theoretic relations among answer sets.

recordSet.name: lcquad_en
recordSet.description: Rows from LC-QuAD.tsv. Each row contains one benchmark item with four related natural-language questions.

field.name: lcquad_en/Q3
field.description: Question expected to target a subset or constrained variant of Q1's answers.

field.name: lcquad_en/Q4
field.description: Complementary question paired with Q3 so that Q3 and Q4 partition or complete Q1 depending on the benchmark item.

recordSet.name: qawiki_en
recordSet.description: Rows from qawiki.tsv. Each row links one or two source entities to four related questions and a relation type label.

field.name: qawiki_en/q1
field.description: Optional URI-like anchor for the first seed entity.

field.name: qawiki_en/q2
field.description: Optional URI-like anchor for the second seed entity.

field.name: qawiki_en/Q3
field.description: Question targeting a constrained subset of Q1.

field.name: qawiki_en/Type
field.description: Relation type code used by the benchmark authors.

field.name: qawiki_en/type_legend_note
field.description: Auxiliary note column whose header and first rows encode the legend for the Type labels.

recordSet.name: spinach_en
recordSet.description: Rows from spinach.tsv. Each row includes a source SPARQL identifier plus four related questions and an optional type label.

field.name: spinach_en/usparql
field.description: Identifier for the SPARQL seed query or source example.

field.name: spinach_en/Q3
field.description: Question targeting a constrained subset of Q1.

field.name: spinach_en/type
field.description: Optional relation type label as stored in the TSV.

recordSet.name: synthetic_en
recordSet.description: Rows from synthetic.tsv. Each row is a synthetic benchmark item with four related questions.

field.name: synthetic_en/Q3
field.description: Question targeting a constrained subset of Q1.

rai:dataCollection: The English benchmark was assembled as a small collection of question-answering evaluation tables. Items were curated from benchmark-style sources such as LC-QuAD, QAWiki-related materials, SPARQL-based question seeds, and author-created synthetic prompts. Each item was normalized into a four-question template (Q1-Q4) designed to probe equivalence, containment, and complement relations between answer sets.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw inputs are natural-language questions and, for some subsets, entity or SPARQL identifiers used as anchors during curation.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Source materials were converted into tab-separated files with a consistent Q1-Q4 layout.
Question sets were manually or programmatically rewritten so that Q2 is intended as an equivalent reformulation of Q1, while Q3 and Q4 express constrained or complementary variants.
Auxiliary source-specific metadata was retained only when needed for traceability, such as entity anchors or SPARQL identifiers.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The benchmark does not provide per-item human preference labels. Instead, its supervision signal is structural: each item encodes intended semantic relations among question answer sets, such as equivalence between Q1 and Q2 or subset/complement relations involving Q3 and Q4.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation of large language models for consistency across semantically related question variants.
Analysis of answer-set equivalence, containment, and decomposition behavior in question answering.
Benchmarking prompting, retrieval, or post-processing methods that aim to improve semantic consistency.
Not recommended as a standalone training corpus for open-domain QA because it is small, purpose-built, and relation-focused rather than coverage-focused.
rai:dataBiases: Because part of the benchmark is derived from existing knowledge-base QA resources, topic coverage is likely skewed toward entities, relations, and domains that are well represented in Wikidata-style sources.
The English-only release may favor models and prompting strategies that perform better on English phrasing and on Western or highly documented entities.
Synthetic items may encode author assumptions about what constitutes a clean subset or complement relation, which can make them easier or more regular than naturally occurring user queries.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is designed for consistency analysis, not for measuring broad factual QA quality or real-user utility.
Some semantic relations are approximate and depend on pragmatic interpretation of natural-language questions, so benchmark items may still contain ambiguity.
The small size of each source file limits fine-grained subgroup analysis and makes the dataset sensitive to a few difficult or noisy items.
The benchmark should not be used to make claims about demographic fairness because it does not contain the coverage or annotations needed for that purpose.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The released TSV files are question-only benchmark items and are not intended to contain personal or sensitive user data. Some questions may refer to public figures or public entities drawn from knowledge bases.
rai:dataSocialImpact: A positive use of this dataset is improving the reliability of QA systems by testing whether they behave consistently under semantically related prompts. A negative use would be over-claiming that success on this benchmark implies general truthfulness, safety, or fairness. The dataset should therefore be treated as a targeted diagnostic benchmark rather than a comprehensive certification tool.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: This release is a static benchmark snapshot tied to the submission package dated 2026-05-04. Future changes should be versioned by publishing a new Croissant file and updating the dataset URL to the corresponding anonymous archival or hosting location.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.name: Source curation and benchmark assembly
prov:wasGeneratedBy.description: Authors selected source question materials and reorganized them into a unified English benchmark collection under data/Dataset/en.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.name: Question normalization
prov:wasGeneratedBy.description: Each benchmark item was normalized into Q1-Q4 columns so that related questions expose expected answer-set relations such as equivalence, subset, and complement.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.name: Synthetic benchmark generation
prov:wasGeneratedBy.description: A subset of the English benchmark was author-generated to create controlled question sets with intended set-theoretic relations.
